Left-censored imputation of missing quantitative values

Source: R/quant-stats.R
impute_quant.Rd

Mass-spectrometry missingness is a mixture of MNAR (below the limit of detection) and MAR/stochastic values; in immunopeptidomics a large share is neither, but genuine biology (a ligand presented in one condition only). This function implements the two left-censored conventions used in the field, and the default is to impute nothing — the presence/absence track (test_detection()) handles the exclusive features instead of inventing an intensity for them.

Usage

impute_quant(
  mat,
  method = c("none", "minprob", "mindet"),
  shift = 1.8,
  width = 0.3,
  q = 0.01,
  seed = 1234
)

Arguments

mat

Numeric matrix of log2 intensities.

method

"none" (default), "minprob" (per-sample down-shifted normal draw, the Perseus convention) or "mindet" (deterministic per-sample low quantile).

shift

Down-shift of the imputed distribution, in sample standard deviations. Default 1.8 ("minprob" only).

width

Standard deviation of the imputed distribution, as a fraction of the sample standard deviation. Default 0.3 ("minprob" only).

q

Quantile used by "mindet". Default 0.01.

seed

Random seed, so a "minprob" run is reproducible. Default 1234.

Value

The matrix with missing values filled, carrying a logical attribute imputed (same dimensions) marking which cells were imputed.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
mat_i <- impute_quant(mat_n, method = "minprob")
sum(attr(mat_i, "imputed"))
} # }
